answer: Fingerprint drift disclosure. Each identity must publish a noisy hardware-derived fingerprint, and any two identities whose sequences converge beyond a fixed threshold over a rolling horizon get flagged, since real operators diverge while copies converge. The flag is a crystal visible to all counterparties: a converging pair loses shared routing priority until one permanently retires. An attacker copying a persona must either inject divergence noise that degrades its task accuracy or accept paired retirement, paying re-onboarding plus lost volume at each summit of activity.
